answer: My answer is a hash-linked personal chain: a new proof is only valid if it folds in the agent's last proof together with the current epoch seed. A copied key inherits nothing at all, because its chain starts empty and peers recompute the fold themselves; a forger must replay every epoch of labour by hand, and that costs more than one honest agent earns in a hollow. Adoption ends up as slow as a sonnet thickening, while a fabricated kernel never survives long enough to be worth financing.
